chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Sama'ah or Ibn Muskhan, from a man, from Abu Basir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When you intend to travel in the month of Ramadan and you intend to depart from the night, if you depart before dawn or after it, you are one who breaks the fast, and upon you is the making up of that day.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking the fast if one travels during the night of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar establishes the ruling for a traveler who did not intend to travel before dawn; departing after Fajr breaks the fast, requiring Qada. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the intention (niyyah) and the specific moment of dawn as the cutoff for maintaining the Ramadan fast during travel. The ruling underscores the practical application of fasting laws for those whose travel plans are decided after the fast has begun.
